The fit gives Dq ≈ 1845 cm⁻¹ (10Dq ≈ 18 450 cm⁻¹) and B ≈ 727 cm⁻¹, with C = 4.5B ≈ 3272 cm⁻¹.

The complex is low-spin d⁶ with a ¹A₁g ground state. The two bands are therefore ¹A₁g→¹T₁g (16 474 cm⁻¹) and ¹A₁g→¹T₂g (25 381 cm⁻¹). The bands were fitted with the full d⁶ ligand-field matrix, including configuration interaction, using the tanabesugano fit tool with the low-spin state selected.

The tool fixes C rather than the ratio C/B, so I ran it at three values of C and solved for the self-consistent point:

| Fixed C (cm⁻¹) | Fitted Dq (cm⁻¹) | Fitted B (cm⁻¹) |
|---|---|---|
| 2600 | 1805.8 | 719.8 |
| 2900 | 1823.5 | 723.1 |
| 3200 | 1840.8 | 726.4 |

B rises almost linearly with C, by about 0.0111 cm⁻¹ per cm⁻¹ of C. Imposing C = 4.5B in that relation gives B ≈ 727 cm⁻¹ and C ≈ 3272 cm⁻¹. Interpolating Dq at that C gives about 1845 cm⁻¹. These values reproduce both bands to within about 0.01 cm⁻¹.

Two bands fix two parameters exactly, so the fit has no spare degrees of freedom. The result is therefore only as good as the assumed C/B = 4.5.
